text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Most companies unworried about knock-on effects from the Securitel affair. (p1)
- Number of mergers and acquisitions involving Dutch companies falls sharply in first half of 1997. (p3)
- Pharmaceutical producer and wholesaler OPG sees 1997 first half net drop nine percent due to pricing law and start-up losses. (p4)
- Investment group Robeco's assets rise 15 pct to Dfl 93.5 bn in first six months of 1997. (p9)
- KLM pilots get support from U.S. pilots' association in fight against economy measures. (p2)
- Japan's writing material plant Sakura takes over Bruynzeel's pencil unit. (p2)
- Builder Ballast Nedam gets patent on movable lawns and stands for stadiums. (p23)
- Bank insurer Fortis subsidiary GWK chief steps down half a year early. (p25)
- Food company Nutricia abandons plans for taking over Sweden's Vitamex. (p7)
- Port services firms Deka and ECT take over bankrupt Bell Lijn. (p9)
